text:
devon: heads-up: ran into a weird read-after-write on a live prefetched prefix during an aggressive eviction test. filing quick notes before i write a longer postmortem.

maria: what happened?

devon: sequence: write -> immediate handoff triggered by balancer -> read from new owner returned stale value. not every run, only under tight timing.

kai: any logs or markers present?

devon: logs show old owner cleared cache slot, set an eviction marker, then lost its lease unexpectedly (leader failover). new owner started serving before reconciler ran.

maria: that suggests marker-clear race vs lease revocation. do we treat marker removal as secondary to lease CAS?

alex: short idea: make marker removal require a successful CAS of the old-lease token. if lease gone/changed, keep marker until reconciler confirms.

kai: downside: markers lingering if old node crashes hard. need TTL + reconciler. also avoid marker-on-every-evict for hot churn.

ops-bot: deploy-bot suggests metrics: ["evict_marker_set","evict_marker_cleared_failed_cas","handoff_reads_with_marker","reconciler_repair_runs"]. recommend alert if handoff_reads_with_marker > 0.01% of reads for a prefix. :bell:

maria: also add a litmus: write -> force handoff -> immediate read from new owner should always reflect write. include leader-failover-in-the-middle variant.

devon: agreed. for rollout we should gate on zero regressions across the litmus under chaos (leader restarts, node kills).

kai: implementation note: encode owner-epoch and lease-id in the marker so reconciler can decide whether to repair or extend drain. keeps decisions deterministic.

alex: one more: keep fast-path evict (no marker) for non-hot prefixes; only attach marker when prefix had a recent mutation or the write-rate exceeds threshold. reduces churn.

maria: good tradeoff. ok devon, please capture this and open an RFC follow-up + test vectors. i'll coordinate ops playbook for reconciler behavior.

devon: will do. ping when draft is up. :thumbsup:
